scope: The preserved b21 complete candidate owns the same modern Backpack/campaign/workspace/vessel fields as the current candidate and includes local road recovery and the jointly solved approaches. It passes 2618 source checks, complete Monaco assembly and native Baltimore junction driving. It remains an emergency save-compatible fallback with known desktop performance limitations, not a substitute for final candidate acceptance. Production 5.5.1 is the upgrade starting point. Before promotion, build and verify this exact fallback with production configuration and complete the released/candidate/fallback-write/candidate-return save roundtrip.

app/js/reality-capture/rdt-building-inde.review: Cooperative construction/validation of a transient nearest-building index. Preserves identity/coordinate edit detection, nearest ordering and cancellation. No saved data.

app/js/reality-capture/runtime.js.review: Awaits bounded capture selection under world/refresh/list identity guards. Same approved-representation endpoint and publication contract; no persistence changes.

app/js/terrain/far-field.js.review: Smaller frustum-culling cells for the same complete regional instance population. No geometry source, collision, identifier or save changes.

app/js/world/linear-feature-presentation.review: Yields between individually clipped paths and bounded numeric copy loops. Same complete rendered geometry and terrain/road authority; transient scheduling only.

config/scene-resource-budgets.json.review: Evidence-backed named Baltimore collider baseline for authored quay/venue fixtures and repaired approaches. No runtime or save protocol change; timing, coverage and retention gates remain unchanged.

app/js/physics/building-collision.js.review: Identical horizontal and vertical predicates, candidate order and collision responses. Rejects geographically distant colliders before evaluating vertical properties, reducing measured temporary allocation. No collision data, geometry, persistence or backend protocol changes.

app/js/world/building-body-geometry.js.review: Uses optional bounded private construction storage with disjoint attribute views. Exact geometry bytes, normals, UVs, transforms, footprint data, clones and edit behavior are preserved. No saved data.

app/js/world/building-facade-layout.js.review: Uses the geometry-owned construction allocator when available, preserving separate ranges, all facade values, and independently owned standalone publication. No visual, persistent or backend schema changes. Facade attribute writes now avoid per-triangle/per-vertex temporary arrays; 24 captured before/after byte fixtures preserve geometry attributes and facade plans exactly.

config/performance-budgets.json.review: Documented acceptance-policy revision: desktop average floor30FPS replaces the dated43.65 snapshot, consistent with the owner priority. All frame-time/hitch, coverage, memory and rendering budgets unchanged. Verification configuration only, no runtime/save/backend change.

app/js/terrain/tile-request-lifecycle.js.review: Consumer deadlines and AbortSignals retire only their own subscriptions. The existing cache owner retains actual source timeout, retry, eviction and world teardown. Transient loading behavior only; no saved fields or network protocol changes.

app/js/terrain/tiles.js.review: Uses the subscription-only waiter and removes the conflicting 2.4-second consumer failure authority. Actual source deadline, three-attempt retry ceiling, cache limit and generation teardown stay unchanged. No saved data.

app/js/terrain/location-world.js.review: Comment clarifies the shared terrain owner; publication order and ten-second wait are unchanged. No persisted data or geometry change.

app/js/structure-semantics/numeric-scrat.review: Bounded, explicitly borrowed numeric scratch pages for synchronous compilation. Nested calls have separate pages; completed profiles use independent publication buffers. At most one MiB is retained by each compiler pool. No saved data or network change.

app/js/structure-semantics/geometry.js.review: Polyline distance arithmetic and Float32 rounding are unchanged. The caller can explicitly provide temporary storage; ordinary callers retain independent arrays. No geometry or persistence semantics change.

app/js/world/compiler/ordinary-street-pr.review: The same ordinary-street alignment solver receives an explicit optional storage allocator. Exact Float32/Float64 values and grade rules remain unchanged; no persistent fields change.

app/js/world/compiler/transport-surface-.review: The same surface, bridge and tunnel solvers receive explicit scratch allocation. Computation order and numeric precision are unchanged; published output is copied before scratch reuse. No persistence change.

Temporary solver storage remains scoped scratch; initial and reconciled published profiles can use bounded append-only pages without aliasing or detaching. Final packed profiles retain all numeric fields. Tunnel terrain probes use the corrected shared physical roof footprint. No saved data or protocol changes.

app/js/world/retired-building-buffers.js.review: Private construction ranges share bounded pages until their geometry owners retire. Unbatched survivors copy exact attribute bytes into independent storage, preventing page pinning; final batches, clones and neighboring geometry remain valid. No persistence or building identity changes.

app/js/world/load-building-pass.js.review: Owns separate near/mid construction arenas, closes them on success or failure, and finalizes standalone attributes after batching. Complete world coverage, semantic rules, building identities and saved data remain unchanged.

app/js/world/load-geometry.js.review: Passes the optional construction arena into generated mid-LOD bodies and their existing fallback. It does not change geometry, material selection, location identity or saved state.

app/js/structure-semantics/numeric-publi.review: Append-only bounded publication pages owned by a compilation. Published views are disjoint and never recycled or detached; only the current page is held by the allocator. No persisted fields or transport topology change.

app/js/structure-semantics.js.review: Passes explicit optional compilation storage through to the existing canonical profile compiler. Standalone callers retain independent storage. No saved fields or protocol change.

app/js/structure-semantics/classificatio.review: Preserves an explicit service=parking_aisle distinction in derived structure semantics. Does not alter source tags, tunnel classification, topology or persisted fields.

app/js/world/compiler/tunnel-envelope.js.review: Parking passages use the existing minimum walkable clearance independently of burial depth. Roof sweep width now matches the actual 2 cm lining offset plus 35 cm portal rim, instead of a fictitious 95 cm envelope. No source data or saved fields change.

app/js/world/compiler/tunnel-obstruction.review: Foundation and overhead-road overlap use the shared physical roof envelope. Buildings actually touched by the shell retain hard clearance bounds; adjacent buildings outside it no longer depress connected streets. No persisted fields change.

app/js/world/compiler/tunnel-system-mode.review: Containment and portal placement use the same corrected roof extent as obstruction and profile compilation. Existing shell/portal authority and data ownership remain intact; no persistence change.

app/js/world/compiler/transport-structur.review: Parking tunnel specification reads the canonical parking clearance. Other road/bridge specifications are unchanged. Derived model only; no persistence or backend changes.

app/js/world/structure-aware.js.review: One explicit append-only publication store per structure compilation, shared across provisional reconciliation passes and released after final packing. No global allocation owner or terrain/topology policy changes. No persistence changes.

app/js/world/load-road-pass.js.review: Initial road compilation uses a pass-owned bounded publication store across cooperative yields. All accepted profiles and source coverage are retained; no player data or road identity changes.

app/js/world/load-linear-runtime.js.review: Immediate linear-feature compilation passes a bounded publication store explicitly to each record. Standalone additions remain independently allocated. All feature identity/access/topology and saved data are unchanged.

app/js/world/traversal.js.review: Temporary per-feature path distances use ordinary double-precision JS numbers rather than native backing buffers. Node positions, source intervals, one-way edges, weights and published route graphs are unchanged. No saved data.

app/js/engine/vehicle-road-attitude.js.review: Four private double-precision JS height values replace one native buffer per NPC contact solve per frame. Sampling order, iterative contact math, reentrant callbacks, final pose and anomaly records are unchanged. No persistence change.

app/js/world/load-roads.js.review: Creates the retained facility terrain callback in the stable loader scope instead of the per-load source context. Same dynamic terrain method, arguments, receiver and return value. Current-source retained-allocation comparison releases about 128 MB including raw regional and building-provider records. No geometry, coverage, persisted state or backend contract changes; native pacing still requires verification.

app/js/terrain/geographic-ring-index.js.review: Optional append-only publication storage for the same Float64 geographic edges and Uint32 bins. Exact crossing expressions and fallback order preserved; immutable edge count avoids retaining the input ring. No data/coverage/save changes.

app/js/terrain/far-field-mapped-context..review: Each loaded land/water context owns bounded append-only pages for immutable ring acceleration data. Release drops only allocator references; retained views are never recycled or detached. Geometry, holes, land classification and coverage unchanged.

app/js/terrain/rebuild.js.review: Published Float32 road-width samples use bounded append-only pages scoped to terrain publication and preserved through later region arrivals. Width calculation, rounding, rendered/physical road surfaces and region retirement unchanged. Unmarked ground roads additionally release temporary dense lane-marking samples; canonical roads, road-index ordering, rendered surfaces and collision coverage remain unchanged.

app/js/discovery/runtime.js.review: Guards unchanged text and three owned HTML sections using UI-instance state. Does not change finding/mission receipt writers, Journal, Backpack, campaign or account persistence. Same controls and changed-message updates verified by the first-session journey.

app/js/world/compiler/accepted-ground-se.review: Reconciles accepted complete overlapping transport geometry across roads and pedestrian/connector collections after ground selection. Only transient world publication ownership changes; missing, partial and rejected sources retain fallback coverage. No saved schema or transaction changes.

app/js/world/compiler/transport-junction.review: Uses the accepted physical connection graph for shared road heights across source providers. Rejects missing, incomplete or unconnected height owners. Runtime world surfaces rebuild per location; persisted player records and save versioning are unchanged. Rolling back restores the earlier road geometry and its known limitations.

app/js/world/compiler/transport-network-.review: Prevents the expanded mixed-source endpoint match from connecting explicitly different at-grade levels. Transient topology only; same source identifiers and saved-data owners.

app/js/world/fixed-regional-structures.j.review: Retires generalized transport geometry only when complete accepted exact coverage is proven, including curved approaches and pedestrian structures. Explicit layers, incomplete/parallel geometry and missing-source fallbacks remain. No player data mutation or migration.

app/js/world/vector-resolution-ownership.review: Adds an opt-in curved-segment coverage proof for fixed regional conflation. Default ordinary vector-road matching is unchanged. Pure geometry ownership; no save fields.
